text:
Harper Lin: Quick question for hiring ops: can we change the auto-enroll deferral on a per-offer basis? Candidate requested 8% default instead of 5%. Need to know vendor process so recruiting can confirm in offer.

Noah Kim: Yep, vendor supports per-employee default via an override. BrightPlan needs a one-off enrollment override submitted before the employees first payroll. It's a CSV with emp_id, effective_date, deferral_percent.

Harper Lin: Does that override persist with auto-escalation or is it a one-time seed?

Jorge Ramirez: It seeds the starting deferral. Auto-escalation still applies unless you submit an escalation opt-out flag. If you want to bypass escalation, include escalate=false in the override.

BenefitsBot: Reminder: default company match is 100% up to 3% + 50% of next 2% (max 4%). Vesting: 25% at 12 months then monthly to 48 months.

Harper Lin: Good to know. Another ask from recruiting: candidate with existing 401k wants to roll it into our plan during onboarding but also needs to set Roth contributions. Can they roll pre-tax funds and elect Roth for future deferrals simultaneously? Any tax caveats?

Noah Kim: Yes. Rollovers are independent of future elections. They can do a trustee-to-trustee rollover of pre-tax funds and still elect Roth for new deferrals; note rollover amount remains pre-tax unless they do an in-plan conversion (taxable event).

Jorge Ramirez: Add: if they request an in-plan Roth conversion of rolled-in pre-tax funds, that triggers a taxable distribution and needs a signed conversion form and payroll tax coordination. Recommend they talk to a tax adviser.

Harper Lin: Also asked about part-time employees (less than 30 hrs) and match eligibility. Recruiting wants language.

Ivy (Payroll): Plan rule: eligibility requires averaging at least 20 hours/week over lookback period. If eligible, match is prorated by eligible pay and applied per payroll. For transfers from contractor, send contractor-hours CSV for manual eligibility check.

Harper Lin: Payroll cutoff for elections to be active on first check?

Ivy (Payroll): Cutoff: benefits elections and overrides must be submitted to payroll 10 business days before start to hit first paycheck. If late, elections start the next payroll cycle; employee can do an after-tax contribution and claim adjustment later, but payroll cannot retroactively reclassify a processed check.

Harper Lin: We had a candidate who enrolled in a full FSA during OE and then tried to open HSA midyear. Does the system prevent that? Any guidance for offering limited-purpose FSA?

Noah Kim: BrightPlan flags incompatible elections. Payroll enforces at contribution time and will block HSA pre-tax deductions if a full FSA is active. Recommend that employees who want HSA choose limited-purpose FSA or delay FSA start. Recruiting should advise: "If you plan to use HSA, select limited-purpose FSA or defer FSA enrollment."

Jorge Ramirez: One operational note: if they need an exception (e.g., paperwork timing), benefits can open a BrightPlan support ticket with tag "redwood-payroll-impact" and payroll can process a manual override with employee-signed acknowledgment.

BenefitsBot: FYI: 2025 HSA limits: $3,850 individual / $7,750 family, +$1,000 catch-up for 55+. Payroll enforces limits; employee excess contributions handled per vendor process.

Harper Lin: Last thing: can recruiting tell candidates about loan availability? Some ask right away.

Noah Kim: Loans allowed per plan rules after meeting participation/service requirements (typically 12 months). Vesting acceleration doesn't change service requirement. Use conservative language: "Loans subject to plan rules and service requirements."

Harper Lin: Thanks everyone 44d I'll update the offer checklist: include CSV override steps, rollover instructions, limited-purpose FSA note, payroll cutoff, and loan caveat.

Ivy (Payroll): I'll paste an example override CSV in Confluence and add the payroll contact. Also: send any vendor tickets to payroll@redwood.com with subject line "BrightPlan override - new hire" for faster routing.

Harper Lin: Perfect, appreciate it!
